title: 2012 AMC 12A Problem 3
statement: A box \(2\) centimeters high, \(3\) centimeters wide, and \(5\) centimeters long can hold \(40\) grams of clay. A second box with twice the height, three times the width, and the same length as the first box can hold \(n\) grams of clay. What is \(n?\)

solutions.text:
The second box has \(2 \times 3 \times 1 = 6\) times the volume of the first, so it holds \(6\) times as much clay.

Therefore \(n = 6 \cdot 40 = 240.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The capacity is proportional to the volume
